the_hub_launch_bug.symptom: User launched Forge and every workspace said the tool 'isn't ported into Forge yet', even though app_window.py had started all three backends successfully and status.json said available:true for all three.
the_hub_launch_bug.root_cause: static/index.html is loaded over file://, and it read its availability data with fetch('status.json'). A file:// page has an opaque origin, so WebKit rejects that fetch as cross-origin. The catch block set status = {}, every lookup came back undefined, and the code path for 'undefined' was the not-ported placeholder.
the_hub_launch_bug.fix: app_window.py now also writes static/status.js containing `window.FORGE_STATUS = {...}` and the shell reads that global -- a <script> tag has no cross-origin restriction. allow-file-access-from-file-urls / allow-universal-access-from-file-urls are also set on the WebView as belt-and-braces for any future fetch.
the_hub_launch_bug.lesson: Anything the file:// shell needs from disk must arrive as a <script> global, not a fetch.

bugs_found_and_fixed: MediaForge Storage Tools opened TWO EventSource connections to the same scan job (the exact bug class PROGRESS.json warned about, which had been fixed in NovelForge's audiobook panel but not here). Job events flow through a single-consumer queue.Queue, so the second connection stole roughly half the stream including, unpredictably, the terminal 'done' event -- the scan would appear to hang forever. Fixed by adding an onLog callback to MediaForge's streamJob so one connection serves both the log text and the status line.

Both backends' SSE endpoints could end a stream with NO terminal event: if a job finished before anyone listened, or an earlier connection consumed its terminal event, the generator just returned. EventSource then auto-reconnected forever while the panel's buttons stayed disabled. Both now synthesize the terminal event from the job's real status, and both frontends' onerror handlers additionally poll GET /api/jobs/{id} to settle the UI instead of ignoring the error.

MediaForge's SSE progress coalescing emitted the kept progress tick AFTER the non-progress events in the same batch, and dropped it entirely when 'done' landed in the same batch. Now flushed in order.

MediaForge's four hand-rolled setInterval job polls (duplicates, dedupe scan, organiser preview, organiser apply/revert) had no error branch: a failed job fell through to a result fetch that 400s, then threw on undefined fields, so a failure showed as a silent JS crash or a bogus success toast. Replaced with one pollJob() helper that reports failures.

Both frontends read `(await res.json()).detail` on every failed request. An unhandled server exception returns plain text, so res.json() threw and replaced the real error with a JSON parse error. Both now use an errText(res, fallback) helper that falls back to the HTTP status.

NovelForge interpolated user-typed project and series names straight into URL paths unencoded. A name containing # or ? silently truncated the request path. All of them now go through encodeURIComponent, via a pu()/projUrl() pair.

NovelForge built the Home project rows and MediaForge built the organiser preview rows with innerHTML templates containing user-controlled filenames and titles -- a name containing < or & corrupted the markup. Both now build those rows from DOM nodes with textContent.

NovelForge's Export button reported 'Export finished' and then threw on data.results even when the export had failed; same missing res.ok guard on the research lookup and series create. All guarded now.

NovelForge's audiobook Build button dereferenced abVoiceMap, which is null unless the Export tab was opened while a project was already open -- opening the project afterwards produced a TypeError. It now loads the voice map on demand.
NovelForge jumped the user to the Story tab the moment generation finished (openProject() always called selectTab('story')), hiding the finished stream. openProject now takes {switchTab}.
MediaForge's manga fetch dereferenced j.result.title with no guard on a job that ended without a result.
Both backends kept every job object forever. Added _prune_jobs(), which keeps the 20 most recent finished jobs so a client can still ask how one ended.

white_on_white_fix.symptom: White text on white background across most MediaForge tabs.
white_on_white_fix.root_cause: WebKitGTK renders native controls -- <select> popups, number spinners, checkboxes, <audio> players, scrollbars -- with the GTK theme rather than page CSS. Under a light GTK theme the dropdown popup is white, while the near-white `color` the page sets on <select> is inherited by its <option>s. MediaForge has 30 select elements against NovelForge's 11, which is exactly why it showed up 'in most of the tabs' there. `color-scheme` was declared nowhere.

session_3_work.css_regression_found_and_fixed: Immediately after the refactor the user reported NovelForge and MediaForge rendering entirely black-on-white while AI Studio looked correct. Cause: the header comment in shared/forge.css contained a NESTED /* ... */ (an illustrative snippet inside the explanation). CSS comments do not nest, so the inner close ended the block early, the parser's error recovery then consumed the text that followed AND the :root block behind it, and the palette never applied. AI Studio was unaffected because it still declares its own :root inline. Fixed by rewriting the header without an embedded snippet; the file now carries a warning about it. Verified by actually serving both backends and parsing the delivered stylesheet: :root survives comment-stripping with --bg, --text, --panel, --accent and color-scheme intact, and html/body still resolves background to var(--bg). LESSON: after editing either shared file, run a comment-balance audit -- a stylesheet that 404s and one that parses into nothing look identical from the server side, since both return 200.

session_5_work.why_it_is_a_forge_app_not_just_an_artifa: A published Artifact runs under a CSP that blocks all fetch/XHR to anything but the page itself, so it can never reach Jan on localhost:1337. The Jan-driven game therefore needs a local backend. The same static/index.html runs in both places: it calls GET /api/status once on load, and when that 404s (Artifact) or reports jan:false, the LLM game falls back to a built-in template brain and stays fully playable.

the_four_games.standing-wave: Ported and polished from the earlier standalone artifact. Live cymatics field driven by the FFT of the user's MP3; bright antinodes drain energy, dark nodal lines are safe. Polish this pass: a 4s grace period, a colour-coded reading ring around the node that teaches the danger threshold, floating +score text on mote pickups, darker LUT mids for readability, slower difficulty ramp (90s), gentler drain (46/s) and stronger regen (15/s).
the_four_games.aphelion: Gravity slingshot. Drag to aim; the predicted trajectory is integrated with the SAME stepper the probe uses and turns cyan when the shot reaches the beacon / red when it hits a body. That preview is also what makes the game robust to blind physics tuning -- the player aims by the drawn path, not by absolute constants. Procedural levels from a seeded mulberry32, moving bodies from level 4, probe budget with +1 per level cleared.
the_four_games.zero-beat: Waveform matching. Slide amplitude and phase per harmonic until the difference trace flattens under tolerance. The monitor tone is two 220Hz oscillators detuned in proportion to the error, so a match is a literal zero beat. DOM range inputs rather than canvas dials -- keyboard-accessible for free and reliable on touch.
the_four_games.hearsay: The Jan game. Five crew on a relay station, a 40-minute hole in the outbound log, 24 moves before the evening boat. Verbs: ask where/who/opinion, PRESS a contradiction the notebook has flagged, and LEAK what one crew member said to another.

session_5_work.the_rule_that_keeps_hearsay_coherent: THE ENGINE DECIDES WHAT AN NPC SAYS; JAN ONLY DECIDES HOW THEY SAY IT. Culprit, motive, true locations, who-saw-whom and the one keystone observation that breaks the cover story are all generated deterministically in JS. On each question the engine computes the answer CONTENT and passes it to Jan as 'convey exactly this, in your own voice'; the notebook logs the engine's version, never the model's. So a small local model cannot corrupt the mystery, and the game is winnable with Jan switched off. Each NPC's prompt also carries their own prior claims and what others have told them, which is what makes them stay consistent -- the felt 'memory'.
session_5_work.jan_integration: apps/arcade/web_app.py proxies POST /api/jan/chat to JAN_BASE_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1). It auto-detects whichever model Jan currently has loaded via GET /v1/models, cached 60s -- hardcoding a model id breaks the first time the user swaps models in Jan's UI. Overridable with JAN_BASE_URL / JAN_MODEL env vars.

Zero Beat and Hearsay build their own DOM into #gameUI; the other two are pure canvas. No libraries at all -- Canvas 2D + Web Audio only.

waveguide_generator_bug.symptom: Roughly 2% of generated levels at level 6+ were impossible to solve.
waveguide_generator_bug.root_cause_1: Levels were built by construction, but a later turn-mirror can land on a cell an EARLIER segment already crossed. The beam then deflects on that first pass, so the constructed walk and the true beam path diverge.
waveguide_generator_bug.root_cause_2: Decoy mirrors were excluded from the CONSTRUCTED path rather than the TRACED one, so decoys landed on the true beam. A mirror deflects at both of its rotations, so no amount of rotating the other pieces could recover -- unsolvable by construction.
waveguide_generator_bug.fix: build() now (1) constructs, (2) applies the intended solution and TRACES it, rejecting and retrying up to 40 times if the receivers do not light, (3) places decoys only after that trace and never on a cell the traced beam visits, (4) re-scrambles until the board is not already solved, and (5) falls back to a provably solvable one-mirror board if all 40 attempts fail.

session_12_work.theme: New app: PulseForge (:8436, order 9) -- a music-video / visualizer studio, built to help the user make money on YouTube.
session_12_work.what_it_is: Feed it a song plus optionally a background image / AI backdrop / pixel-sprite pack / folder of video clips; pick a scene and an output format; get a YouTube-ready MP4 with visuals cut and modulated to the music. session_12_work.architecture: Almost everything is an ffmpeg job. pulseforge/analyze.py decodes audio -> numpy per-frame features (energy, 12 log bands, sub, centroid, onset, beat) with the band-split/beat math ported from Arcade (no librosa). A scene is one file in pulseforge/scenes/ that yields RGB frames from those features (drawn with vectorised numpy/Pillow at an internal <=1080p buffer, so ffmpeg upscales for 4K cheaply) OR, for the montage family, returns an edit decision list. render.py pipes frames to ffmpeg (scale/mux/loudnorm/encode), handles the seamless-loop two-pass, and builds the montage trim->fit->concat filter_complex. Adding a scene = one file + one line in scenes/registry.py.

session_14_work.theme: PulseForge v3 -- the living-still studio. A background that mostly holds still while marked parts of it move, over a playlist of songs and a list of backgrounds with transitions. This is the v3 the user asked for at the end of session 13, plus the region/effect system underneath it.
session_14_work.the_core_idea: A shot's motion is LOOP-EXACT by construction: every effect and emitter takes its phase from pulseforge/looping.py's LoopClock, which snaps any requested period to a whole number of cycles inside the shot's loop. Nothing uses raw time. So a shot is BIT-IDENTICAL at t=0 and t=loop_seconds, which buys two things at once: the loops are clean (the user asked for 'much cleaner' loops), and the renderer only computes ONE loop of numpy frames and lets ffmpeg -stream_loop repeat that bed for as long as the shot holds. An hour-long mix over four backgrounds costs four short renders instead of ~108,000 frames. A shot set to mode='live' opts out and renders every frame so it can react to the song.
session_14_work.new_modules: looping.py (LoopClock). imageops.py (bilinear sample/displace, box_blur, periodic_noise that tiles exactly). masks.py (polygon points or a brush PNG -> feathered float mask, cached, + bbox so effects only touch their own region). layers.py (Camera + Backdrop: background image plus stacked transparent PNGs). motion/ REGISTRY of 9 region effects: water, sway, flow, sky_clouds, shimmer, glow_pulse, flicker, breathe, frames (the user's own artwork). emitters/ REGISTRY of 11: particles (fully configurable), rain, snow, dust, fireflies, bubbles, stars, leaves (leaf/petal), birds, fish, sprites (own artwork or a ForgeArtData pack). scenes/living.py (the flagship scene; composes in depth order then grades). sequence.py (joins the playlist, places shots, per-song drawtext captions with enable windows). autoregions.py. presets.py (11 looks). artsource.py (folder of PNGs / GIF / sprite strip). tools/shot.py.

session_15_work.modulation_is_the_architectural_one: Any numeric parameter may be {base, mod, amount, period, shape} instead of a number. It is unpacked in merge_params() -- the single choke point both registries already resolve through -- so it works for all 11 effects and 11 emitters and anything added later, with zero per-effect code. LFO sources run off the LoopClock, so a MODULATED PARAMETER STILL LEAVES THE LOOP SEAM BIT-IDENTICAL (tested). Audio sources (energy/sub/onset/centroid) only mean anything in live mode and the UI says so.
session_15_work.parallel_rendering: pulseforge/bedworker.py: each loop bed renders in its own SUBPROCESS driven by a JSON job file. Deliberately not multiprocessing -- fork from the web app's render thread is the deadlock-prone path Python now warns about, and spawn/forkserver both re-import __main__ which fails depending on how the parent was started (it failed immediately when driven from a heredoc). Only loop beds are parallelised; live beds need megabytes of numpy analysis. Falls back to sequential on any failure. Measured 33.9s -> 18.8s for four beds (1.80x). Byte-identical output when the encoder thread count matches. Worker count is a Setting, default 3 of 12 cores so the machine stays usable.
session_15_work.bug_fixed_rain_fell_upward: The emitters treated angles as if the y-axis pointed up, but image rows grow downward -- so every 'falling' default (rain 285, snow 268, leaves 260) was inverted, and `flow` scrolled the wrong way too. There is now one imageops.direction_vector() with an intuitive compass (0 right, 90 up, 270 down) used by every effect and emitter, plus regression tests asserting rain moves down and bubbles move up. A still frame of drifting particles looks identical either way, which is why nothing caught it.
session_15_work.bug_fixed_silent_fallback: The parallel bed job dict carried the numpy analysis the worker never reads, so JSON serialisation failed and EVERY render silently fell back to sequential. session_16_work.video_backgrounds: pulseforge/videosource.py. A shot's background can be a clip. Frames are STREAMED from one ffmpeg pipe (one frame of memory, not a gigabyte), and because almost nothing loops on its own, the stretch just past the bed is decoded separately and cross-dissolved into the bed's first frames. Measured: on a deliberately non-looping clip the wrap went from 2.9x a normal frame step to 1.5x. Camera, regions, emitters, DoF and grade all still apply on top.
session_16_work.ambience: pulseforge/ambience.py generates rain / fire / vinyl / wind / waves with numpy -- shaped noise plus transients, ends cross-faded so ffmpeg can loop 30s under an eight-hour video.
